title: Below the average
prompt: Show the name of employees earning below the overall average, A to Z.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY name;
SELECT name FROM employees ORDER BY name;

title: Customers without a Kitchen buy
prompt: Show the name of customers who've never bought a Kitchen product.
hints: Careful with customers who have no orders.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Kitchen');

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Kitchen');
SELECT name FROM customers;

title: Course average spread
prompt: Show the highest course average minus the lowest course average, rounded to 1 decimal, as spread.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT ROUND(MAX(average) - MIN(average), 1) AS spread FROM (SELECT AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(grade) - MIN(grade), 1) AS spread FROM enrolments;
SELECT ROUND(MAX(average), 1) AS spread FROM (SELECT AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id);

title: Hottest in its city
prompt: Show the id of each city's hottest reading, including ties.
hints: Compare each reading with its own city.
solutions: SELECT r.id FROM readings r WHERE r.temp_c = (SELECT MAX(x.temp_c) FROM readings x WHERE x.city = r.city);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT r.id FROM readings r WHERE r.temp_c = (SELECT MAX(x.temp_c) FROM readings x);
SELECT city, MAX(id) AS id FROM readings GROUP BY city;

title: Spend ranking
prompt: Using a CTE of revenue per customer_id (price times quantity), show the id and name of the top-spending customer.
hints: Name the step, join, sort, and limit.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: WITH r AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.id, c.name FROM r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id ORDER BY r.revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.id, c.name FROM r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id ORDER BY r.revenue LIMIT 1;
SELECT c.id, c.name FROM customers c LIMIT 1;

title: All contact points
prompt: Show every known email and phone in one column named contact, removing duplicates.
hints: Stack two columns, and skip NULLs.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT email AS contact FROM contacts WHERE email IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT phone FROM contacts WHERE phone IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT email AS contact FROM contacts UNION SELECT phone FROM contacts;
SELECT email AS contact FROM contacts WHERE email IS NOT NULL;

title: Enrolled but ungraded
prompt: Show the student_ids with an enrolment but never a grade, using a set operation.
hints: Students with any grade get removed.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 6, NULL, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments EXCEPT SELECT student_id FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NULL;
SELECT student_id FROM enrolments INTERSECT SELECT student_id FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;

title: Above-average users
prompt: Show the username of users whose total minutes exceed the average per-user total.
hints: Compare a total with an average of totals.
solutions: WITH t AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN t ON t.user_id = u.id WHERE t.total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM t);

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN t ON t.user_id = u.id;
SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id WHERE s.minutes > (SELECT AVG(minutes) FROM sessions);

title: Unsold share
prompt: Show the percentage of products never sold, rounded to 1 decimal, as unsold_pct.
hints: Count with a subquery, divided by all products.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10, 'Vase', 'Home', 5.0, 2.0);

solutions: SELECT ROUND((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products), 1) AS unsold_pct;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products), 1) AS unsold_pct;
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)) AS unsold_pct;

title: Newest per department
prompt: Show the department_id and name of the most recent hire in each department. Ignore employees with no department.
hints: Compare with the department's latest date.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.department_id, e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.hire_date = (SELECT MAX(x.hire_date) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.department_id, e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.hire_date = (SELECT MAX(x.hire_date) FROM employees x);
SELECT e.department_id, e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.hire_date = (SELECT MIN(x.hire_date) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id);

title: Two kinds of customer
prompt: Show each customer's name and a segment: Buyer if they appear in orders, otherwise Browser, by stacking two queries.
hints: Use UNION ALL with IN and NOT IN.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, 'Buyer' AS segment FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders) UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Browser' FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, 'Buyer' AS segment FROM customers;
SELECT name, 'Buyer' AS segment FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders);

title: Students above their year
prompt: Show the name of students whose average grade is above the average of their year group.
hints: A correlated subquery over a CTE.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO students VALUES (10, 'Iris', 10); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 5, 50, '2024-spring'), (16, 10, 5, 65, '2024-spring');

solutions: WITH a AS (SELECT s.id, s.name, s.year_group, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.year_group) SELECT a.name FROM a WHERE a.average > (SELECT AVG(x.average) FROM a x WHERE x.year_group = a.year_group);

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT s.id, s.name, s.year_group, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.year_group) SELECT a.name FROM a WHERE a.average > (SELECT AVG(x.average) FROM a x);
SELECT name FROM students;

title: Inviters who play
prompt: Show the username of users who've invited someone and also have a session, using INTERSECT on ids and a lookup.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = 7; UPDATE users SET referrer_id = 8 WHERE id = 9;

solutions: SELECT username FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT referrer_id FROM users INTERSECT SELECT user_id FROM sessions);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT username FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT referrer_id FROM users);
SELECT username FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM sessions);

title: Salary gap to the top
prompt: Show each employee's name and how far they are below the highest salary in their department as gap. Ignore employees with no department.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name, (SELECT MAX(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id) - e.salary AS gap FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name, (SELECT MAX(x.salary) FROM employees x) - e.salary AS gap FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id IS NOT NULL;
SELECT e.name, e.salary AS gap FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id IS NOT NULL;

title: Biggest order's customer
prompt: Show the name of the customer who placed the order with the most total units. Break ties with the lowest order id.
hints: Find the order first, then walk to the customer.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (12, 8, 3, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id = (SELECT order_id FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id ORDER BY SUM(quantity) DESC, order_id LIMIT 1);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id = (SELECT order_id FROM order_items ORDER BY quantity DESC LIMIT 1);
wrongSolutions.why: Uses the largest row, not order total

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LIMIT 1;
